No, a court will most likely not enforce the bar against assigning the right to payment. This is a sale of goods, so UCC § 2-210(2) allows a right arising from the seller's due performance of its entire obligation to be assigned despite a contrary agreement, and § 9-406(d) likewise overrides contract terms that prohibit assigning a right to payment. The team note that courts presume a general no-assignment clause reaches payment rights is wrong for this situation. The UCC rules above override that presumption, so the center must pay the assignee once the distributor has performed.

CONFIDENCE: 88
